identity.name: Sorbic acid
identity.chemical_class: Unsaturated monocarboxylic acid (hexadienoic acid); weak-acid preservative

function.mechanism: Weak-acid preservative used to inhibit spoilage microorganisms (especially yeasts and molds), with strongest performance in acidic foods.
common_food_categories: products requiring mold and yeast control

adi.basis: Group ADI for sorbic acid (E200) and potassium sorbate (E202) in EFSA follow-up opinion (2018).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA follow-up concluded no genotoxicity concern for sorbic acid/potassium sorbate and estimated exposure below the ADI at assessed uses.

fda.notes: GRAS when used in accordance with good manufacturing practice; related feed section is 21 CFR 582.3089.

adi.basis: JECFA full ADI listed as 0-25 mg/kg bw/day for sorbic acid.

concerns.summary: Recent prospective cohort analyses reported associations between some preservative additive exposures (including potassium sorbate) and incident cancer/type 2 diabetes, but these are observational and mixture-exposure findings rather than causal proof for sorbic acid alone.

A 2025 systematic review of mammalian-cell studies reported cytogenotoxicity signals for preservatives including potassium sorbate, while EFSA regulatory assessment did not identify a genotoxicity concern for sorbic acid/potassium sorbate at evaluated conditions.

Recent animal and in vitro mechanistic studies reported reproductive, hepatotoxic, and apoptosis-related signals for potassium sorbate (often in combination/high-dose contexts), supporting caution but not establishing risk at typical regulated intake.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA follow-up reported no genotoxicity concern for sorbic acid (E200) and potassium sorbate (E202).
EFSA exposure estimates in the follow-up opinion were below the group ADI of 11 mg/kg bw/day.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA follow-up reported highest high-percentile exposure up to 7.6 mg/kg bw/day, below ADI 11 mg/kg bw/day.

risk_assessment.rationale: E200 remains approved/GRAS, but risk management relies on an explicit ADI and GMP controls, and newer epidemiologic/mechanistic studies create non-zero uncertainty despite no direct regulatory conclusion of harm at current intake levels.
key_factors: EFSA group ADI is numeric (11 mg/kg bw/day), not ADI-not-specified.
EFSA follow-up exposure estimates were below ADI, including high consumers.
Recent cohort and mechanistic studies on preservative exposures (including potassium sorbate) indicate signals that warrant continued monitoring.
